title: Model catalog acceptance scenarios and gradual admission (slimline PRD)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD for a lightweight ("slimline") admission path into the public model catalog for community/open models that are not fully pinned. Purpose: give product and runtime engineers a minimal, testable contract to accept experimental weights while limiting operational risk. This doc defines the required metadata fields, automated sanity-check scenarios, tolerated behavioral deltas, and the staged rollout/rollback acceptance flow. It is intentionally narrower than full onboarding PRDs: focused on runtime assurance signals and deterministic acceptance tests that can be automated in CI and the catalog intake pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Metadata: incoming model submission includes required fields: runtime_hints, tokenizer_profile, known_compat_flags (list), primary_alias, semantic_version, and provenance_url. Missing fields cause triage, not automatic admission.

Sanity suite: every slimline entry must pass an automated runtime smoke test in a simulated Dedicated environment: generation for 3 prompt templates (short, mid, long) with max_tokens=1024 must complete within target latency percentiles (p95 <= baseline * 2) and not exceed memory thresholds for the declared quantization profile.

Behavioral regression threshold: on the provided eval prompt set (50 prompts), response quality measured by current eval harness (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) must not degrade more than 12% relative to the claimed reference model; otherwise the intake is escalated to full PRD intake.

Fallback mapping: catalog entry must define at least one fallback_alias (pinned variant or compatible family) and a fallback_policy (region, capacity, or cost-based). Runtime must be able to route to fallback automatically on OOM/THROTTLE errors within 30s of detection in canary traffic runs.

KV & cache hinting: runtime_hints must include kv_cache_compatibility boolean and recommended prefix_cacheable boolean. If kv_cache_compatibility is false and model is large (>= 13B), admission requires manual sign-off from Applied ML.

Canary rollout: admission to hosted catalog is phased: (1) gated in internal only, (2) 1% external canary for 24h with telemetry checks, (3) 10% for 48h, (4) full public. Observable signals for automatic promotion: error_rate < 0.5% above baseline, cost-per-token delta within acceptable band, and quality regression within threshold. Any breached signal schedules immediate rollback and incident creation.

Audit & provenance: provenance_url must resolve to an artifact (weights manifest or registry) and be captured in catalog metadata. Admission records must generate an immutable audit log entry with submitter, tests run, and verdict that is retained 1 year by default.

Operational playbook: runway for rollback must be under 2 hours with clear playbook steps (re-route, revoke, notify) documented in the catalog entry links section. On-call runbooks must be linked during admission and verified by SRE before promotion to external canary.

Private/Dedicated compatibility: an entry that passes slimline admission for hosted must also be tagged compatibility:private_ok if it has network/resource requirements documented; otherwise private customers default to pinned variants only.

Acceptance gates are automatable: each gate maps to a CI job or catalog pipeline check and returns a deterministic pass/fail event to the intake dashboard. Manual approvals are required only on escalations (failed quality or resource anomalies).
notes: Rationale: many community models are high-value for evaluation but we lack capacity to full-onboard every variant. Slimline admission balances discoverability with operational safety.

Trade-offs: looser behavioral thresholds may surface regressions to users; tighter thresholds increase intake friction. We propose the 12% quality delta as a compromise after benchmarking 24 community models.

Implementation hints for ENG: create a kubernetes-based smoke harness that can claim capacity in a dedicated test pool, run token-limited generation, and surface memory/latency metrics to the catalog API.
SRE ask: add an automated rollback webhook for catalog promotions and a dashboard tile showing canary health for slimline entries.
PM risk: if provenance_url is broken or points to private artifacts, the entry must be marked 'manual-review' and cannot be promoted to external canary.
